description: Manual evidence for an SDK the kit has no conformance driver for (xdrcheck conform siblings --manual FILE). This worked example records a source reading of stellar-dotnet-sdk 17.0.0 for the liquidity-pool asset-order cells; nothing in it was executed. Each cell states the verdict the conformance runner would have given and what the source shows. The format is described in go/internal/conform/siblings/manual.go.
basis: Read at commit 6eea5fcadff5bd64bd418f1995a1c6c1d11055d3 (release 17.0.0): StellarDotnetSdk/Assets/AssetTypeCreditAlphaNum4.cs lines 69-71 and AssetTypeCreditAlphaNum12.cs lines 65-67 order two credit assets with the same code by string.Compare(Issuer, other.Issuer, StringComparison.Ordinal), that is by strkey text; StellarDotnetSdk/LiquidityPool/LiquidityPoolConstantProductParameters.cs lines 29-31 throw ArgumentException when assetA.CompareTo(assetB) >= 0, and FromXdr (lines 97-102) calls that constructor.

cells.observed: The two issuers order differently as strkey text and as XDR bytes, so the constructor's text comparison finds the pair in XDR byte order out of order and throws 'Asset A must be < Asset B (Lexicographic Order).'
The reversed pair is in strkey text order, so the constructor accepts it and the pool ID is derived from parameters stellar-core refuses.
Same comparison as the network-order member: the pair in XDR byte order is refused with 'Asset A must be < Asset B (Lexicographic Order).'
Same comparison as the reversed-order member: the reversed pair is accepted.
CompareTo returns 0 for an asset paired with itself and the constructor throws, as stellar-core requires a strict order.
FromXdr calls the same constructor, so reading the pool-share ChangeTrust of this network transaction throws.
